newsitem.title: UK: Anglian invests more to improve water supply.
newsitem.headline: Anglian invests more to improve water supply.

text.p: Anglian Water Plc said on Tuesday that it plans to spend 34 million stg on improving the security of customer supplies.

The investment will go towards schemes enabling the transfer of surplus water to possible areas of scarcity next summer if winter rainfall is lower than average. The company said rainfall so far this year has been only 67 percent of average.

Anglian said it also plans to spend two million stg annually on reducing leakage and improving customer service. Current leakage is 13 percent compared to a target of 10 percent by the turn of the century.

Full year capital expenditure is expected to be 340 million stg and the company's five year spending proramme is on course, "achieving the required outputs whilst saving 15 percent through efficiencies from project management".
Anglian on Tuesday announced a 5.5 percent rise in first half pre-tax profits to 132.7 million stg and a 14.6 percent hike in the interim dividend to 10.2 pence per share.
"Our dividend increase reflects the continued improvement being made in the efficiency of the regulated business and the board's confidence that further cost savings can be achieved."
